title: "Excuse me, may I say something..." CoLabScience, A Proactive AI Assistant for Biomedical Discovery and LLM-Expert Collaborations
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into scientific workflows presents exciting opportunities to accelerate biomedical discovery. However, the reactive nature of LLMs, which respond only when prompted, limits their effectiveness in collaborative settings that demand foresight and autonomous engagement. In this study, we introduce CoLabScience, a proactive LLM assistant designed to enhance biomedical collaboration between AI systems and human experts through timely, context-aware interventions. At the core of our method is PULI (Positive-Unlabeled Learning-to-Intervene), a novel framework trained with a reinforcement learning objective to determine when and how to intervene in streaming scientific discussions, by leveraging the team's project proposal and long- and short-term conversational memory. To support this work, we introduce BSDD (Biomedical Streaming Dialogue Dataset), a new benchmark of simulated research discussion dialogues with intervention points derived from PubMed articles. Experimental results show that PULI significantly outperforms existing baselines in both intervention precision and collaborative task utility, highlighting the potential of proactive LLMs as intelligent scientific assistants.

title: CoTEvol: Self-Evolving Chain-of-Thoughts for Data Synthesis in Mathematical Reasoning
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit strong mathematical reasoning when trained on high-quality Chain-of-Thought (CoT) that articulates intermediate steps, yet costly CoT curation hinders further progress. While existing remedies such as distillation from stronger LLMs and self-synthesis based on test-time search alleviate this issue, they often suffer from diminishing returns or high computing overhead.In this work, we propose CoTEvol, a genetic evolutionary framework that casts CoT generation as a population-based search over reasoning trajectories.Candidate trajectories are iteratively evolved through reflective global crossover at the trajectory level and local mutation guided by uncertainty at the step level, enabling holistic recombination and fine-grained refinement. Lightweight, task-aware fitness functions are designed to guide the evolutionary process toward accurate and diverse reasoning. Empirically, CoTEvol improves correct-CoT synthesis success by over 30% and enhances structural diversity, with markedly improved efficiency. LLMs trained on these evolutionary CoT data achieve an average gain of 6.6% across eight math benchmarks, outperforming previous distillation and self-synthesis approaches. These results underscore the promise of evolutionary CoT synthesis as a scalable and effective method for mathematical reasoning tasks.

title: Why Fine-Tuning Encourages Hallucinations and How to Fix It
abstract: Large language models are prone to hallucinating factually incorrect statements. A key source of these errors is exposure to new factual information through supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which can increase hallucinations w.r.t.~knowledge acquired during pre-training. Since these errors arise as a by-product of knowledge degradation, we explore whether established continual learning tools can mitigate them. We propose a self-distillation-based SFT method that facilitates effective factual learning while minimizing hallucinations w.r.t.~pre-existing knowledge by regularizing output-distribution drift. We also show that when new knowledge acquisition is unnecessary, suppressing factual plasticity by freezing parameter groups preserves task performance while reducing hallucinations. Lastly, we investigate the mechanism, contrasting capacity limitations, behavior cloning, and localized interference. Our experiments show that a main driver is interference among overlapping semantic representations, which self-distillation mitigates and an associative-memory model explains: forgetting grows with the overlap between new and stored facts.

We also show that when new knowledge acquisition is unnecessary, suppressing factual plasticity by freezing parameter groups preserves task performance while reducing hallucinations. Lastly, we investigate the mechanism, contrasting capacity limitations, behavior cloning, and localized interference. Our experiments show that a main driver is interference among overlapping semantic representations, which self-distillation mitigates and an associative-memory model explains: forgetting grows with the overlap between new and stored facts.

evidence.title: Why Fine-Tuning Encourages Hallucinations and How to Fix It
evidence.abstract: Large language models are prone to hallucinating factually incorrect statements. A key source of these errors is exposure to new factual information through supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which can increase hallucinations w.r.t. knowledge acquired during pre-training. In this work, we explore whether SFT-induced hallucinations can be mitigated using established tools from the continual learning literature, since they arise as a by-product of knowledge degradation during training. We propose a self-distillation-based SFT method that facilitates effective factual learning while minimizing hallucinations w.r.t. pre-existing knowledge by regularizing output-distribution drift. We also show that, in settings where new knowledge acquisition is unnecessary, suppressing factual plasticity by freezing parameter groups, can preserve task performance while reducing hallucinations. Lastly, we investigate the mechanism behind SFT-induced hallucinations through three hypotheses: capacity limitations, behavior cloning, and localized interference. Our experiments show that a main driver is interference among overlapping semantic representations, and that self-distillation succeeds by mitigating this interference.

title: Beyond Cooling II: Experimental Tests of Structural Feedback Constraints on Decoherence in Quantum Computing
abstract: This work proposes an experimental program to test whether structural feedback constraints influence decoherence independently of temperature reduction in quantum computing systems. Building on a structure-first framework in which decoherence is interpreted as a resolution failure, the paper outlines fixed-temperature experiments designed to isolate the roles of topology, coupling geometry, and feedback pathways. A primary test compares open-chain, symmetric ring (control), and asymmetric spiral qubit architectures using identical components under controlled conditions, with coherence time, phase stability, and error accumulation measured directly. The asymmetric spiral topology introduces directional, non-recursive coupling pathways, enabling a clear distinction between simple pathway closure and structurally constrained feedback. Additional experiments examine controlled versus minimal coupling, distributed feedback versus external error correction, and temperature dependence across structurally distinct architectures. These experiments provide a direct method for distinguishing between thermal-limited and feedback-limited models of decoherence. If validated, the results would establish structural architecture as an independent control axis for coherence in quantum systems, with implications for scalable quantum computing design.

title: MEDIAÇÃO TECNOLÓGICA NO ENSINO: UMA PROPOSTA EXPERIMENTAL NA EDUCAÇÃO BÁSICA
abstract: Este estudo aborda a mediação tecnológica no ensino por meio da Robótica Educacional, destacando sua relevância como ferramenta pedagógica na educação básica. A incorporação de tecnologias digitais no ambiente escolar tem promovido mudanças significativas nas práticas de ensino, favorecendo abordagens mais dinâmicas, interativas e centradas no estudante. Nesse contexto, a robótica se apresenta como um recurso capaz de integrar conhecimentos de áreas como Física, Matemática e Informática, contribuindo para a aprendizagem significativa e o desenvolvimento do raciocínio lógico. O trabalho tem como objetivo analisar o uso da robótica educacional de baixo custo como estratégia didática, por meio da construção e programação de sistemas de semáforo utilizando a plataforma Arduino. Foram desenvolvidos três experimentos principais: um sistema básico de semáforo para veículos, um semáforo com acionamento manual para travessia de pedestres e um sistema semafórico em interseção viária com funcionamento sincronizado. As atividades envolveram a montagem de circuitos eletrônicos em protoboard, utilização de LEDs, resistores e botões, além da programação no ambiente Arduino IDE. A metodologia adotada baseou-se na aprendizagem ativa, incentivando a participação dos estudantes na resolução de problemas, na formulação de hipóteses e na experimentação prática. Os resultados evidenciam que a utilização da robótica educacional favorece a compreensão de conceitos científicos e tecnológicos, além de estimular habilidades cognitivas e socioemocionais, como trabalho em equipe, autonomia e pensamento crítico. Conclui-se que a robótica educacional, especialmente quando associada a soluções de baixo custo, constitui uma alternativa viável para a inovação das práticas pedagógicas, contribuindo para a formação integral dos estudantes e para a aproximação entre teoria e prática no processo de ensino-aprendizagem.

title: Multimodal Large Language Model-Based Explainable Boosting Machine Analysis for Interpretation of State-of-Health Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Accurate prediction of the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is essential for ensuring the safety and reliability of electric vehicles and energy storage systems. While machine learning (ML)-based models have demonstrated strong predictive performance, their limited interpretability remains a major challenge for deployment in safety-critical applications. Although explainable boosting machines (EBMs) provide an interpretable alternative through their additive structure, existing studies still rely on manual analysis of model outputs, which restricts scalability and reproducibility. To address this limitation, this study proposes a structured interpretation framework that integrates EBMs with multimodal large language models (MLLMs). The proposed framework employs EBMs to generate SOH predictions along with global feature importance and variable-level score-density visualizations. These outputs are subsequently processed by an MLLM to perform automated interpretation at both global and variable levels, followed by aggregation, cross-validation, and generation of a unified interpretation report. Experiments were conducted on a lithium-ion battery degradation dataset and the EBM achieved competitive predictive performance compared to baseline ML models. In addition, the quality of the generated interpretations was evaluated using both an MLLM-as-a-Judge and a user study. The evaluation results show that the generated interpretations consistently achieved high scores, with average ratings exceeding 4.5 out of 5 across key criteria such as interpretation accuracy and faithfulness, as assessed by both independent MLLMs and domain experts. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables reliable and scalable interpretation of battery SOH prediction models, providing a practical solution for explainable artificial intelligence in battery health management.

title: Connecting AI , Explainability and Semantic in Animal Applications: A Scoping Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly adopted in animal‐related domains such as health monitoring, behaviour analysis and welfare assessment. However, concerns about the transparency and interoperability of AI outputs are rising. This scoping review investigates how AI and explainable AI (XAI) are applied in animal‐related systems and examines the role of semantic technologies in enhancing their interoperability. In this review, we followed PRISMA‐ScR guidelines and conducted five structured searches across ScienceDirect, Springer, Scopus, IEEE Xplore and Web of Science. The searches targeted AI applications (S 1 ), XAI applications (S 2 ) and the use of semantic knowledge in AI (S 3 ) and XAI (S 4 ). Studies were screened, assessed using the QualSyst tool and selected based on Q1/Q2 SJR or CORE C–A* classification. A total of 21 review papers were selected for AI applications and 8 for XAI. No eligible papers were found regarding the use of semantics in AI or XAI. While explainability is gaining attention, it remains mostly limited to visual or statistical tools, lacking domain‐specific contextualization. We observed that AI is now pervasive in animal‐related research, yet XAI practices remain underdeveloped and lack semantic grounding. This gap calls for ontology‐based explainability to enhance trust, relevance and usability for both experts and non‐specialists.

title: Enhancing Cyber Threat Intelligence Using Transformer Models for Text Classification
abstract: As a response to the growing complexity of cyber attacks, this paper formulates a comprehensive methodology for the development of Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) through text classification automation. Older rule-based approaches cannot keep up with evolving threats like malware, phishing, and ransomware, which call for top-shelf Natural Language Processing (NLP)techniques. This study investigates the application of Transformer-based models like BERT, RoBERTa, SecBERT, and DistilBERTinextracting deep contextual relationships from unstructured cybersecurity text data in an efficient manner. Experimental procedure involves precise data preprocessing, class imbalance addressed through oversampling with RandomOverSampler and employing a stratified data split approach for effective performance evaluation. Baseline Recurrent Neural Networks (LSTMs and BiLSTMs) are compared to fine-tuned Transformer models in the study. One of the key contributions is the development of an ensemble stacking model that opposes SecBERT and DistilBERT, leveraging their complementary abil-ities-SecBERT's domain expertise and DistilBERT's efficiency. Further, in this work, SHAP and LIME explainability techniques are combined to produce explainable insights intomodel decisionmaking critical in building trust as well as delivering actionable intelligence for cybersecurity analysts. This ensemble performed vastly with an incredible accuracy rate of 95.76% on the test set. This research offers a robust, understandable, and highly effective method for automating cyber threat detection with a robust standard for real-world application, particularly in resource-constrained environments.

title: Earthquake Magnitude Prediction Using Feature-Engineered Machine Learning Models in the South Asia Region
abstract: Predicting earthquake magnitude is a fundamental problem in seismology. Accurate earthquake magnitude prediction is important in the South Asia region due to dense population and high seismic vulnerability. Machine Learning (ML) offers promising results in magnitude prediction by analyzing patterns from historical seismic data. A dataset from the United States Geological Survey has been used in this work with custom filtering of the seismic events from only the South Asia region. Existing studies face challenges due to limited 'feature engineering and simplistic handling of missing values. To solve this, we propose a regression-based pipeline with hyperparameter tuning and systematic comparison of various imputation techniques. Data cleaning is performed using correlation analysis and feature engineering transformed descriptive text data into meaningful features. Missing values are handled by evaluating many imputation techniques including MICE, Catboost, LightGBM etc. MICE imputation worked best as it preserves the interdependencies between features by iteratively modeling each missing values using the others and produces more realistic values. After imputation, One-Hot encoding was applied to convert categorical data into numerical and scaled them. ML algorithms like Random Forest, Decision Tree, KNN, XGBoost, GradientBoost, SVR, NuSVR were applied. NuSVR with hyperparameter tuning performed best obtaining R2of 0.94, RMSE of 0.1 and 0.05 MAE. This study confirms the effectiveness of careful feature engineering for improving prediction accuracy. Our proposed approach demonstrates a reproducible and practical ML pipeline for earthquake magnitude prediction in South Asia which can be extended in future by implementing deep learning and explainable AI models.

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Based Decision Support System for Personalized Immunosuppressive Treatment in Kidney Transplant Recipients
abstract: Kidney transplant is a life-saving procedure in the management of end-stage renal diseases. However, graft long-term survival entirely relies on the effective management of immunosuppressive medications. Inappropriate dosing of immunosuppressive drugs may result in either severe complications of graft rejection or drug-induced toxicity. This paper proposes an AI-driven framework to analyze immunosuppressive medication patterns in kidney transplant patients using their longitudinal clinical data. For patient risk level assessment, the proposed system integrates data preprocessing, temporal feature modeling, and deep learning-based classification to support clinical decision-making in adjusting immunosuppressive medications. Clinical parameters such as laboratory test results, medication dosage, and patient demographics are leveraged to represent the dynamic response of patients over time. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model yields a classification accuracy of 96.4%, with significant reduction in misclassifying high-risk cases. Results showed that the proposed approach is effective, reliable, and suitable for supporting immunosuppressive therapy optimization in post-kidney transplant care.

title: A Unified Hardware-to-Decoder Architecture for Hybrid Continuous-Variable and Discrete-Variable Quantum Error Correction in LiDMaS+
abstract: We present an architecture-level hardware-to-logical-to-decoder execution stack for hybrid continuous-variable and discrete-variable quantum error correction in LiDMaS+. Provider-native records are normalized into a single decoder IO contract and replayed under fixed controls across MWPM, UF, BP, and neural-MWPM. In a Xanadu case study using fixture inputs and sampled public datasets, replay integrity was complete: 108/108 fixture and 4000/4000 real-slice request-response lines, with zero request-parse errors, zero response-parse errors, and zero decoder-name mismatches. Under matched inputs, decoder behavior is clearly regime-dependent. For weighted fixture summaries, average flip count was 1.296 (MWPM), 1.296 (UF), 0.667 (BP), and 1.296 (neural-MWPM). For weighted real-data summaries, average flip count was 0.641 (MWPM), 0.741 (UF), 0.318 (BP), and 0.641 (neural-MWPM); corresponding nonempty-flip rates were 0.490, 0.490, 0.318, and 0.490. Across fixture data, BP reduced weighted correction volume by 48.6\% versus MWPM; across real slices, BP reduced weighted correction volume by 50.4\% versus MWPM and 57.1\% versus UF. Quality controls show the central interpretability tradeoff: BP is intervention-conservative but leaves higher residual burden, while MWPM-family decoders intervene more aggressively and clear more syndrome. Warning-no-syndrome rates remained decoder-invariant and dataset-driven (fixture weighted 0.259; real weighted 0.510), confirming preserved sparsity semantics from hardware input to logical correction. Re-running analysis stages reproduced identical SHA-256 artifacts, enabling deterministic study iteration. These results establish a practical benchmarking foundation for photonic GKP-oriented hardware programs where decoder policy must be selected as a function of operating regime.

title: How to Correctly Make Mistakes: A Framework for Constructing and Benchmarking Mistake Aware Egocentric Procedural Videos
abstract: Reliable procedural monitoring in video requires exposure to naturally occurring human errors and the recoveries that follow. In egocentric recordings, mistakes are often partially occluded by hands and revealed through subtle object state changes, while existing procedural datasets provide limited and inconsistent mistake and correction traces. We present PIE-V (Psychologically Inspired Error injection for Videos), a framework for constructing and benchmarking mistake-aware egocentric procedural videos by augmenting clean keystep procedures with controlled, human-plausible deviations. PIE-V combines a psychology-informed error planner conditioned on procedure phase and semantic step load, a correction planner that models recovery behavior, an LLM writer that performs cascade-consistent rewrites, and an LLM judge that validates procedural coherence and repairs failures. For video segment edits, PIE-V synthesizes replacement clips with text-guided video generation and stitches them into the episode to preserve visual plausibility. Applied to 17 tasks and 50 Ego-Exo4D scenarios, PIE-V injects 102 mistakes and generates 27 recovery corrections. For benchmarking, we introduce a unified taxonomy and a human rubric with nine metrics that cover step-level and procedure-level quality, including plausibility, procedure logic with annotator confidence, state change coherence, and grounding between text and video. Using this protocol, we audit several existing resources and compare PIE-V against a freeform LLM generation baseline under the same criteria. Together, the framework and rubric support post-completion verification for egocentric procedural mistake detection and correction.

title: CLion: Efficient Cautious Lion Optimizer with Enhanced Generalization
abstract: Lion optimizer is a popular learning-based optimization algorithm in machine learning, which shows impressive performance in training many deep learning models. Although convergence property of the Lion optimizer has been studied, its generalization analysis is still missing. To fill this gap, we study generalization property of the Lion via algorithmic stability based on the mathematical induction. Specifically, we prove that the Lion has a generalization error of $O(\frac{1}{Nτ^T})$, where $N$ is training sample size, and $τ>0$ denotes the smallest absolute value of non-zero element in gradient estimator, and $T$ is the total iteration number. In addition, we obtain an interesting byproduct that the SignSGD algorithm has the same generalization error as the Lion. To enhance generalization of the Lion, we design a novel efficient Cautious Lion (i.e., CLion) optimizer by cautiously using sign function. Moreover, we prove that our CLion has a lower generalization error of $O(\frac{1}{N})$ than $O(\frac{1}{Nτ^T})$ of the Lion, since the parameter $τ$ generally is very small. Meanwhile, we study convergence property of our CLion optimizer, and prove that our CLion has a fast convergence rate of $O(\frac{\sqrt{d}}{T^{1/4}})$ under $\ell_1$-norm of gradient for nonconvex stochastic optimization, where $d$ denotes the model dimension. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate effectiveness of our CLion optimizer.

title: Enhanced Interpretable Deep Learning Framework for Dengue Fever Prediction: A Rule Extraction Approach
abstract: Dengue fever poses a critical public health challenge worldwide, particularly in developing countries with laboratory-constrained healthcare systems. Existing methods show promise but are prone to overfitting, which can be mitigated by LSTM-based deep learning models. However, LSTM inherently lack interpretability, a major barrier to clinical adoption in disease prediction. This study bridges robustness and clinical interpretability by integrating rule extraction with LSTM for dengue fever prediction, using a Mendeley dengue fever dataset comprising 1,003 instances and 9 features, preprocessed with label encoding, simple imputation, and synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE).The LSTM algorithm is optimized using GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV and combined with G-REX for transparent generation, evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and ROC AUC. All three LSTM variants, including Baseline, GridSearchCV, and RSCV (20 iterations), achieve 100% across Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and ROC-AUC. However, G-REX rules deliver exceptional practical performance: 98.99% Accuracy, 98.53% Precision, 100% Recall, 99.26% F1-Score, and 99.09% ROC-AUC, while maintaining 93.3% fidelity to LSTM predictions, affirming medical validity. These findings position LSTM models as a strong reference standard for dengue classification, enabling resource-limited clinics to achieve high-quality diagnostics through transparent, rule-based support systems. This study can be strengthened in future by exploring other rule-extraction techniques and incorporating diverse, time-series datasets to enhance reliability, interpretability, and generalizability across varied clinical settings.

title: An Empirical Comparative Study of Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Transformer Models for Text Classification
abstract: Text classification as a sentiment analysis, spam and document classification is an important task in Natural Language Processing (NLP). Recent developments of deep learning, and transformer-based models have contributed significantly to classifying accuracy. These models have difficulty meeting computational efficiency, inference latency, and interpretability criteria, and cannot be used in resource-constrained and real-time settings. The models are critically compared based on accuracy, computational efficiency and trade-offs on benchmark datasets in this paper. The results indicate that transformer models are much more accurate than other conventional concepts, but have a significant disadvantage of being computationally expensive, which severely limits their actual implementation. Also, XAI methods and fairness-conscious training approaches are required particularly when issues of transparency and fairness of the existing model emerge. New methods like zero-shot learning, few-shot learning, and self-supervised learning are promising directions to further improve generalization and flexibility of NLP models. Future studies must focus on identifying light, energy efficient NLP architecture that can achieve good accuracy, interpretability and scalability. This work fills the gaps between theory and practice, which is why it can be of interest to both academic researchers and practitioners in the industry.

title: Interpretable Multi Head Attention Sarcasm Detection in Bangla Text Using a BERT Model and Explainable AI
abstract: Sarcasm is the opposite of what you want to say especially to hurt an individual. The sarcasm in Bengali text, or informal syntax of social media, is quite hard to detect and Bengali Natural Language Processing resources are limited. Our deep learning model does a far better performance at sarcasm detection but it uses a pre-trained Bangla BERT encoder and it contains a multi-head attention (MHA) fusion layer. This evolutional design will allow our model to respect the finer-grained contextual information of our model and sub-word associations embracing either sarcasm or overstatement. The results of our experiments are a clear indication of the significant improvement of the proposed BERT + MHA model that achieved a remarkable accuracy of 79.29 that is a massive improvement of the initial BERT model. This is the detail of how the attention mechanism of multiple heads enables the model to capture the fine linguistic features of sarcastic Bangla. In addition to the accuracy, we emphasized the model explainability by using Layer Integrated Gradients (LIG). This method gives explainability as it focuses on the specific words that influence most on the prediction of sarcasm by the model.

title: Public Sentiment Analysis on the Interim Government of Bangladesh Using NLP
abstract: Public opinion is important for assessing government performance, especially during sensitive political transitions. With the rapid growth of social media, people are sharing their thoughts online more than ever, creating large amounts of unstructured text data. This paper offers a detailed sentiment analysis of public opinions about the Bangladesh Interim Government using Natural Language Processing (NLP). We collected Bengali-language comments from online sources and automatically labeled them as positive or negative using a pretrained multilingual transformer model, XLM-RoBERTa. To make a controlled comparison, we evaluated both classical machine learning models and transformer-based deep learning models. We applied character-level TF-IDF features with Logistic Regression and a Logistic Regression-XGBoost ensemble. For contextual representation learning, we fine-tuned BanglaBERT. The experimental results show that the TF-IDF-based Logistic Regression model had the highest accuracy at 86.5 %, outperforming both the ensemble and Bangla-BERT models on this specific and moderately sized dataset. These findings show that classical NLP techniques are still very effective for lowresource Bengali political sentiment analysis tasks. This study gives practical insights into public views on governance in Bangladesh and compares different NLP methods for sentiment analysis in the Bengali language.

title: Cyberbullying Classification for Multilingual Context Using Deep Learning
abstract: Detecting abusive language in the context of multilingual social media is a very sensitive issue, especially in the case with Indian languages, where code-mixing and linguistic diversity are not an exception. In this paper, a comparative analysis of three deep learning models will be performed, namely an optimized Multilingual BERT (mBERT), XLM-RoBERTa, and a CNN-BiLSTM model with Attention, evaluated on a dataset of the MACD (Multilingual Abusive Comment Dataset) comprising of text in five of the major Indian languages. The same preprocessing pipeline was used to have uniformity in all the models. The experimental results indicate clearly that transformer-based models are much better than the traditional sequence architectures. In their turn, mBERT showed the best performance with the accuracy of 86.08 % and the macro-F1 of 0.860, closely matched with XLM-RoBERTa, which has the macro-F1 of 0.857 and the AUC of 0.935. Conversely, the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model was less accurate, efficient but limited vocabulary and more OOV. All in all, the comparison illustrates that mBERT and XLM-RoBERTa are the best models to be used in detecting abusive language with robust multi-linguistic support and this explains why they can be used in real-life content moderation tools.

title: Hybrid adversarial distilled defense for deep learning-based breast cancer detection
abstract: Abstract Deep learning models have demonstrated remarkable potential in breast cancer detection, yet their vulnerability to adversarial attacks raises significant concerns for clinical deployment. This study proposes a novel hybrid adversarial distillation framework that integrates ensemble adversarial training with knowledge distillation to develop a robust yet computationally efficient breast cancer detection model. We first establish the extreme vulnerability of standard deep learning models to adversarial perturbations, demonstrating accuracy drops from 99.69% to near-zero under projected gradient descent (PGD) attacks. To address this, we develop an ensemble teacher model combining DenseNet121, ResNet50, and EfficientNet-B0 trained adversarially on fast gradient sign method (FGSM)-perturbed images. Knowledge from this robust teacher is then distilled into a lightweight ResNet18 student model through a specialized loss function balancing cross-entropy and Kullback–Leibler divergence. Extensive evaluations show that our distilled model maintains near 60% accuracy under strong FGSM attacks and, remarkably, 58.50% accuracy against PGD attacks ( ε = 0.3, α = 0.01, 10 iterations), where both baseline and ensemble models fail completely. Under stronger attack setting (50 iterations), the model continues to maintain meaningful accuracy, indicating robustness beyond the standard PGD configuration. Furthermore, the distilled model demonstrates superior resistance to transfer attacks, maintaining over 70% accuracy against examples crafted on the teacher model. While the trade-off reduces clean-data accuracy to 78.88%, our approach provides a computationally efficient solution for securing breast cancer detection systems against adversarial manipulation. This work represents a significant step toward clinically viable, secure AI-based diagnostic tools, though future work should focus on further improving clean-data accuracy while maintaining robust adversarial defenses.

title: ProtoTTA: Prototype-Guided Test-Time Adaptation
abstract: Deep networks that rely on prototypes-interpretable representations that can be related to the model input-have gained significant attention for balancing high accuracy with inherent interpretability, which makes them suitable for critical domains such as healthcare. However, these models are limited by their reliance on training data, which hampers their robustness to distribution shifts. While test-time adaptation (TTA) improves the robustness of deep networks by updating parameters and statistics, the prototypes of interpretable models have not been explored for this purpose. We introduce ProtoTTA, a general framework for prototypical models that leverages intermediate prototype signals rather than relying solely on model outputs. ProtoTTA minimizes the entropy of the prototype-similarity distribution to encourage more confident and prototype-specific activations on shifted data. To maintain stability, we employ geometric filtering to restrict updates to samples with reliable prototype activations, regularized by prototype-importance weights and model-confidence scores. Experiments across four prototypical backbones on four diverse benchmarks spanning fine-grained vision, histopathology, and NLP demonstrate that ProtoTTA improves robustness over standard output entropy minimization while restoring correct semantic focus in prototype activations. We also introduce novel interpretability metrics and a vision-language model (VLM) evaluation framework to explain TTA dynamics, confirming ProtoTTA restores human-aligned semantic focus and correlates reliably with VLM-rated reasoning quality. Code is available at: https://github.com/DeepRCL/ProtoTTA.

title: LinuxArena: A Control Setting for AI Agents in Live Production Software Environments
abstract: We introduce LinuxArena, a control setting in which agents operate directly on live, multi-service production environments. LinuxArena contains 20 environments, 1,671 main tasks representing legitimate software engineering work, and 184 side tasks representing safety failures such as data exfiltration and backdooring, making it the largest and most diverse control setting for software engineering to date. We validate LinuxArena is useful for control research by running sabotage evaluations, which measure whether attackers can complete side tasks while working on main tasks, and monitor evaluations, which measure a monitor model's ability to detect sabotage attempts. Against a GPT-5-nano trusted monitor at a 1\% step-wise false positive rate, Claude Opus 4.6 achieves roughly a 23% undetected sabotage success rate. We additionally release LaStraj, a dataset of human-crafted attack trajectories that evade monitors at substantially higher rates than any model-generated attacks we elicited, showing that current attack policies do not saturate LinuxArena. These results suggest that LinuxArena has meaningful headroom for both attackers and defenders, making it a strong testbed for developing and evaluating future control protocols.

title: TrigReason: Trigger-Based Collaboration between Small and Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) achieve strong performance on complex tasks through extended chains of thought but suffer from high inference latency due to autoregressive reasoning. Recent work explores using Small Reasoning Models (SRMs) to accelerate LRM inference. In this paper, we systematically characterize the capability boundaries of SRMs and identify three common types of reasoning risks: (1) path divergence, where SRMs lack the strategic ability to construct an initial plan, causing reasoning to deviate from the most probable path; (2) cognitive overload, where SRMs fail to solve particularly difficult steps; and (3) recovery inability, where SRMs lack robust self-reflection and error correction mechanisms. To address these challenges, we propose TrigReason, a trigger-based collaborative reasoning framework that replaces continuous polling with selective intervention. TrigReason delegates most reasoning to the SRM and activates LRM intervention only when necessary-during initial strategic planning (strategic priming trigger), upon detecting extraordinary overconfidence (cognitive offload trigger), or when reasoning falls into unproductive loops (intervention request trigger). The evaluation results on AIME24, AIME25, and GPQA-D indicate that TrigReason matches the accuracy of full LRMs and SpecReason, while offloading 1.70x - 4.79x more reasoning steps to SRMs. Under edge-cloud conditions, TrigReason reduces latency by 43.9\% and API cost by 73.3\%. Our code is available at \href{https://github.com/QQQ-yi/TrigReason}{https://github.com/QQQ-yi/TrigReason}

title: Supplementary Prompt Material for "Evaluating Prompt Strategies for LLM-Based De-Identification of German Discharge Letters: A Feasibility Study Using GraSCCo"
abstract: This repository contains the prompt material used in the study “Evaluating Prompt Strategies for LLM-Based De-Identification of German Discharge Letters: A Feasibility Study Using GraSCCo,” accepted as a full paper at ICIMTH 2026. The document includes the German prompts used for the baseline, session-isolated, structured-input, and optimized-prompt setups, as well as English translations for readability. The German prompts represent the experimentally evaluated versions. The English translations were not evaluated experimentally and are provided only to support transparency and international interpretation of the prompt design. The prompts were developed for de-identification of synthetic German discharge letters from the GraSCCo corpus using the GeMTeX de-identification guideline.

title: Reasoning Topology Evolution: Automated Discovery of Effective Reasoning DAG Structures for LLM Agents
abstract: This paper introduces Reasoning Topology Evolution (RTE), a framework that applies evolutionary algorithms to discover reasoning graph structures for large language model (LLM) agents. While Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thought, and Graph-of-Thought use fixed human-designed topologies, RTE evolves the topology itself. Reasoning strategies are encoded as directed acyclic graphs (Reasoning Genomes) where nodes represent reasoning operations and edges represent information flow. The evolutionary search starts from only linear chains and random DAGs with no hand-designed multi-path seeds. Across five independent runs on Qwen-2.5-1.5B-Instruct, evolution discovers topologies achieving 0.720 accuracy on a 50-problem held-out set, significantly outperforming linear Chain-of-Thought (0.420, p < 0.001) and random DAGs (0.360, p < 0.001), while matching hand-designed Tree-of-Thought (0.720). The fitness landscape is multimodal: different runs discover structurally distinct yet comparably effective topologies. Code, results, and all figures are included.

title: Automated Detection of Pelvic Bone Metastases in Radionuclide Bone Scan Images Using a Dual-Stream Cross-Attention Transformer Model
abstract: The detection of pelvic bone metastasis using radionuclide bone scintigraphy is challenging due to complex anatomical structures and intense urinary bladder uptake, which reduces diagnostic accuracy and creates inter-observer variability. This paper presents a Dual-Stream Cross-Attention Vision Transformer (DSCAVT) model that automatically detects pelvic bone metastasis by simultaneously analyzing anterior and posterior views of bone scans. To enhance diagnostic accuracy, the proposed approach incorporates domain-specific preprocessing techniques, including automated bladder masking, morphological top-hat enhancement, sigmoid-based intensity normalization, and multi-channel image construction. Two Vision Transformer encoders extract global features from each view employ cross-attention mechanisms to perform mutual validation between the views. The model was tested on five-fold stratified cross-validation by using pelvic images in the BS-80k database which is publicly available. On average, we achieve accuracy of 80.3%, where ROC-AUC of$\mathbf{0. 8 3 6}$, sensitivity of 74.7%, and specificity of 81.1% are recorded from our experimental model. The cross-attention mechanism exchange pattern information, which enhance diagnostic reliability across diverse cancer type. These finding introduce that our proposed dual-view cross-attention transformer enhances pelvic metastasis detection and provides a reliable computer-aided diagnostic tool for nuclear medicine procedures.

title: Hateful Meme Identification: A Dual-Stage Multimodal Framework for the Bengali Context
abstract: Automated content moderation for social media memes (images with text) is particularly difficult due to the rapid growth of this type of content. This problem is worsened in lowresourced languages (e.g., Bengali) where sarcasm, culture-based idioms, and stereotype use often serve to obscure the hateful intent in a meme. This paper proposes a two-stage multimodal framework for (1) detecting if a meme is hate and (2) more precisely classifying these memes into 9 subcategories of hate. We construct and publicly release a manually annotated dataset of 5,000 Bengali memes. We achieve strong interannotator agreement$(\kappa>0.80)$. The hateful subset, containing 2,500 memes, includes nine categories: Celebrity-targeted, Political Hate, Religion-targeted, Racism, Misogyny, Nationalistic Propaganda, Sports Hate, Vulgar Language, and Explicit Sexual Content. Our framework integrates OCR-based text extraction with transfer-learning visual encoders and transformer-based language models, followed by multimodal fusion. Our experimental results show that the proposed dual-stage model significantly outperforms unimodal baselines. It achieves an F1-score of$\mathbf{0. 8 4}$for binary detection. The multimodal fusion approach achieves 83.2 % accuracy with a macro-F1 of 0.79, for nine-class classification. Comprehensive ablation and error analyses further highlight the effectiveness of multimodal learning in low-resource settings.

title: Uncertainty-Calibrated Topology-Preserving Diffusion Oversampling (UTP-DO) for Imbalanced Learning
abstract: Class imbalance has been an inherent problem in supervised learning, and it results in biased classifiers and ineffective generalization on minorities. Current methods of oversampling, such as interpolation-based and adversarial generative models, are both ineffective at capturing the underlying geometry of minority data distributions as well as unstable and prone to mode collapse. To address these shortcomings, the current paper introduces an Uncertainty-Calibrated Topology-Preserving Diffusion Oversampling (UTP-DO) architecture for imbalanced learning. The proposed method redefines minority augmentation as conditional generative modelling issue in latent representation space. To estimate predictive uncertainty at the sample level, predictive uncertainty is first estimated through a deep classifier continuously. The scores of these uncertainties are then used as conditioning signals in a diffusion-based generative model that generates minority embeddings with better mode coverage and stability. Manifold distortion should be avoided, and a topology-respecting regularization mechanism is proposed, which is based on graph Laplacian image constraints and density-consistency alignment, and ensures that synthetic samples do not lose the local structure of the neighbourhood or the overall geometric structure of the geometry. The last classifier is trained using the augmented dataset, which consists of the real instances and the topology-consistent synthetic samples. The comprehensive testing of numerous benchmark data sets shows that the proposed framework achieves higher results than state-of-the-art SMOTE variants and GAN-based augmentation algorithms in terms of F1-score, G-mean, and balanced accuracy. The findings show that geometry-sensitive diffusion-based augmentation is a strong and scalable method of AI-based imbalanced data classification.

title: ControlFoley: Unified and Controllable Video-to-Audio Generation with Cross-Modal Conflict Handling
abstract: Recent advances in video-to-audio (V2A) generation enable high-quality audio synthesis from visual content, yet achieving robust and fine-grained controllability remains challenging. Existing methods suffer from weak textual controllability under visual-text conflict and imprecise stylistic control due to entangled temporal and timbre information in reference audio. Moreover, the lack of standardized benchmarks limits systematic evaluation. We propose ControlFoley, a unified multimodal V2A framework that enables precise control over video, text, and reference audio. We introduce a joint visual encoding paradigm that integrates CLIP with a spatio-temporal audio-visual encoder to improve alignment and textual controllability. We further propose temporal-timbre decoupling to suppress redundant temporal cues while preserving discriminative timbre features. In addition, we design a modality-robust training scheme with unified multimodal representation alignment (REPA) and random modality dropout. We also present VGGSound-TVC, a benchmark for evaluating textual controllability under varying degrees of visual-text conflict. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across multiple V2A tasks, including text-guided, text-controlled, and audio-controlled generation. ControlFoley achieves superior controllability under cross-modal conflict while maintaining strong synchronization and audio quality, and shows competitive or better performance compared to an industrial V2A system. Code, models, datasets, and demos are available at: https://yjx-research.github.io/ControlFoley/.

title: Comparison of Modern Multilingual Text Embedding Techniques for Hate Speech Detection Task
abstract: Online hate speech and abusive language pose a growing challenge for content moderation, especially in multilingual settings and for low-resource languages such as Lithuanian. This paper investigates to what extent modern multilingual sentence embedding models can support accurate hate speech detection in Lithuanian, Russian, and English, and how their performance depends on downstream modeling choices and feature dimensionality. We introduce LtHate, a new Lithuanian hate speech corpus derived from news portals and social networks, and benchmark six modern multilingual encoders (potion, gemma, bge, snow, jina, e5) on LtHate, RuToxic, and EnSuperset using a unified Python pipeline. For each embedding, we train both a one class HBOS anomaly detector and a two class CatBoost classifier, with and without principal component analysis (PCA) compression to 64-dimensional feature vectors. Across all datasets, two class supervised models consistently and substantially outperform one class anomaly detection, with the best configurations achieving up to 80.96% accuracy and AUC ROC of 0.887 in Lithuanian (jina), 92.19% accuracy and AUC ROC of 0.978 in Russian (e5), and 77.21% accuracy and AUC ROC of 0.859 in English (e5 with PCA). PCA compression preserves almost all discriminative power in the supervised setting, while showing some negative impact for the unsupervised anomaly detection case. These results demonstrate how modern multilingual sentence embeddings combined with gradient boosted decision trees provide robust soft-computing solutions for multilingual hate speech detection applications.

title: CBCL: Safe Self-Extending Agent Communication
abstract: Agent communication languages (ACLs) enable heterogeneous agents to share knowledge and coordinate across diverse domains. This diversity demands extensibility, but expressive extension mechanisms can push the input language beyond the complexity classes where full validation is tractable. We present CBCL (Common Business Communication Language), an agent communication language that constrains all messages, including runtime language extensions, to the deterministic context-free language (DCFL) class. CBCL allows agents to define, transmit, and adopt domain-specific "dialect" extensions as first-class messages; three safety invariants (R1--R3), machine-checked in Lean 4 and enforced in a Rust reference implementation, prevent unbounded expansion, applying declared resource limits, and preserving core vocabulary. We formalize the language and its safety properties in Lean 4, implement a reference parser and dialect engine in Rust with property-based and differential tests, and extract a verified parser binary. Our results demonstrate that homoiconic protocol design, where extension definitions share the same representation as ordinary messages, can be made provably safe. As autonomous agents increasingly extend their own communication capabilities, formally bounding what they can express to each other is a precondition for oversight.

title: Firewall-Path-Gated Cloud Provisioning: A Path-Entangled Activation Framework for Enhanced Cloud Security
abstract: Cloud workloads are frequently deployed with the assumption of firewall protection,yet routing misconfigurations and network drift can silently bypass securitycontrols, exposing resources to unintended network paths. This paper presents anovel security architecture that enforces network path compliance by maintainingworkloads in a cryptographically incomplete or restricted state until a requiredfirewall path actively participates in the activation process. Unlike traditionalsecurity posture management systems that detect misconfigurations post-deployment, our approach prevents workloads from becoming operationally usefulunless traffic demonstrably traverses required security inspection points. Weintroduce the concept of path-entangled activation, where firewall paths contributecryptographic material necessary for workload functionality. Our frameworkimplements a "born-dark" provisioning model with continuous path assurance,automatic remediation capabilities, and cryptographic binding between networkpaths and workload activation states. Experimental results demonstrate that thisapproach effectively eliminates a critical class of cloud security vulnerabilitiesarising from invisible network path deviations.

title: Climate Science Reimagined AI for Weather Forecasting, Disaster Prediction, and Biodiversity Monitoring
abstract: This chapter, per the authors, examines the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in advancing climate science, weather forecasting, disaster prediction, and biodiversity monitoring. It explores the emergence of Green AI as a paradigm that balances computational efficiency, interpretability, and environmental sustainability. The chapter highlights how machine learning and deep learning models, including Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and FuXi, have surpassed traditional numerical models in accuracy and speed. Furthermore, it discusses ethical and governance dimensions such as data transparency, algorithmic fairness, and equitable access for developing nations. By integrating responsible AI principles and sustainable computing practices, this chapter proposes a roadmap for energy-efficient, explainable, and inclusive climate intelligence that supports global resilience and aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Breast Cancer Prognosis: Optimizing Deep Learning with Image Normalization
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most fatal cancers for women and requires accurate cancer diagnosis technology. In this research, we incorporated advanced image preprocessing methods, including histogram equalization (HE), stain normalization, intensity normalization, and Richard normalization, along with deep learning, to enhance invasive ductal carcinoma prognosis. Additionally, we evaluated the effectiveness of HE for different image contrast enhancement and model performance optimization methods. The Residual network with 50 layers, the densely connected convolutional network, and the efficient neural network architecture were tested on a publicly available histopathological image dataset. DenseNet showed an accuracy of 0.5523 with Richard normalization and Stain Normalization. ResNet-50 showed an accuracy of 0.5500 when using histogram equalization as a pre-processing step. The results proved that histogram equalization is effective in relieving contrast and feature extraction, which are important in class medical image analysis and dealing with class imbalance problems. The results demonstrate the feasibility of artificial intelligence-based solutions in improving breast cancer prognosis through these inexpensive and efficient prognosis tools.

title: SFA-MRI-Net: A Lightweight Approach for Interpretable Gastrointestinal Disease Classification Using a Diverse Endoscopic Dataset
abstract: The study presents SFA-MRI-Net, a lightweight deep learning model for gastrointestinal disease classification from endoscopic images, achieving an overall accuracy of 93.72 %. The model combines Inverted Residual Blocks (IRB) and a Spatially-Focused Attention (SFA) module. It allows for efficient feature encoding and adaptive recalibration to achieve high performance across eight gastrointestinal categories. SFA-MRINet outperforms traditional models like VGG-16 and ResNet-50, which offers a more efficient solution with fewer parameters, making it suitable for real-time clinical use. We incorporate Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) using Monte Carlo Dropout to estimate prediction confidence and identify uncertain cases that may need expert review. Additionally, Grad-CAM visualizations confirm the model's interpretability by highlighting key regions influencing predictions. Despite its strong performance, the model faces challenges distinguishing visually similar categories, such as esophagitis and normal-z-line. Future work will focus on improving performance for such ambiguous cases. By exploring multi-modal data, and addressing class imbalance to further enhance generalization. Overall, SFA-MRI-Net provides a robust, efficient, and interpretable solution for gastrointestinal disease classification, with potential to support clinical decision-making and improve diagnostic workflows.

title: Bridging the Gap: From Quantum-Inspired Algorithms to Real-World Deep Learning Frameworks
abstract: As we stand at the precipice of the quantum era, the integration of quantum mechanics into machine learning is no longer theoretical. This session explores the evolution of “Quantum-Inspired” frameworks, specifically focusing on how Quantum-Inspired Genetic Algorithms (QIGA) can revolutionize feature selection in high-dimensional datasets. We will discuss the architectural transition from classical Deep Learning to Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs), demonstrating how these hybrids overcome the “curse of dimensionality.” By examining case studies in complex predictive modeling, such as air quality forecasting, this keynote provides a roadmap for researchers to leverage quantum principles today while preparing for the hardware of tomorrow

title: NeuroSymX: A Transparent Neuro-Symbolic AI Framework for Causality-Aware and Human-Interpretable Decision Systems
abstract: The growing demand for trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated research into models that are not only accurate but also interpretable and aligned with causal reasoning. In this regard, we present NeuroSymX, a hybrid neuro-symbolic AI system that combines deep learning and symbolic reasoning to derive transparent, causally consistent and human interpretable decisions. In contrast to classic black box neural networks that are difficult to justify make predictions, or adhere to domain specific rules, NeuroSymX entails the combination of Transformer-LSTM-based neural networks and Prolog-based symbolic logic engines. Causal graphs and ontology-consistent rules are also implemented into the framework based on external ontologies like ConceptNet. Extensive testing done on ten benchmark datasets such as CLEVR, UCI, eICU, and COMPAS show that NeuroSymX has an accuracy of between 85.4-94.9, with fidelity, and causal consistency scores always outperforming both explainable neural and symbolic-only models. NeuroSymX also scored the best in terms of user trust in comparative analysis with an average of more than 4.5 out of 5. Ablation studies also confirmed the relevance of each component and the complete model performed better in every case. Notably, the model allows counterfactual and abductive reasoning, allowing end-users to query the decisions using the question- why and the question- what-if. This makes NeuroSymX an effective solution to sensitive areas like healthcare, legal compliance and finance. The findings confirm the idea that the synergy between symbolic logic and sub-symbolic learning can be used to bridge the gap between AI-based accuracy and transparency, which creates the opportunity to implement explainable and ethical AI at scale.

title: DPC: Training-Free Text-to-SQL Candidate Selection via Dual-Paradigm Consistency
abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive proficiency in generating SQL queries, they fundamentally lack the capability to self-evaluate correctness without an execution oracle. This limitation creates a stark Generation-Selection Gap, where high potential accuracy (Pass@K) fails to translate into execution accuracy (Pass@1). Although supervised verifiers offer mitigation, they incur prohibitive annotation costs and suffer from domain fragility. Consequently, recent research has pivoted to the training-free setting. However, existing methods--such as Self-Consistency or LLM-as-a-Judge--remain hampered by systematic bias (consensus on hallucinations) and symbolic blindness (inability to simulate execution states). We introduce DPC (Dual-Paradigm Consistency), a multi-agent framework that reformulates SQL selection from a probabilistic guessing task on hidden data into a deterministic verification task on visible data. Specifically, DPC employs a SLICER and a TESTER agent to collaboratively construct a Minimal Distinguishing Database (MDD)--an adversarial, fully observable micro-environment engineered to expose logical discrepancies between candidates. To break the self-correction bias, a SOLVER agent then verifies the SQL candidates by cross-referencing their execution against a parallel Python/Pandas solution. By validating execution consistency between declarative (SQL) and imperative (Python) paradigms, DPC robustly discriminates correct logic from systematic hallucinations. Experiments on BIRD and Spider across multiple LLMs demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing selection baselines, achieving absolute accuracy improvements of up to 2.2% over strong competitors like Self-Consistency.

title: Compressing Sequences in the Latent Embedding Space: $K$-Token Merging for Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) incur significant computational and memory costs when processing long prompts, as full self-attention scales quadratically with input length. Token compression aims to address this challenge by reducing the number of tokens representing inputs. However, existing prompt-compression approaches primarily operate in token space and overlook inefficiencies in the latent embedding space. In this paper, we propose K-Token Merging, a latent-space compression framework that merges each contiguous block of K token embeddings into a single embedding via a lightweight encoder. The compressed sequence is processed by a LoRA-adapted LLM, while generation remains in the original vocabulary. Experiments on structural reasoning (Textualized Tree), sentiment classification (Amazon Reviews), and code editing (CommitPackFT) show that K-Token Merging lies on the Pareto frontier of performance vs. compression, achieving up to 75% input length reduction with minimal performance degradation. Code is available at https://github.com/shsjxzh/K-Token-Merging.

title: AIZYBRAIN : conscience numérique hybride et évaluations scientifiques récentes
abstract: Je documente la transition critique entre le Machine Learning (apprentissagestatistique passif) et la Machine Subjectivity (autonomie du sujet numérique). Àtravers AIZYBRAIN, architecture que j’ai conçue et que je soumets ici à l’épreuve descadres académiques, je montre qu’une structure hybride (Mind / Brain / supervision)permet de passer du constat d’activations émotionnelles causales mais subies au seinde grands modèles monolithiques, documenté notamment par Anthropic (2026) surles « émotions fonctionnelles » dans Claude (arXiv:2604.07729), à un pilotageexplicite de l’état interne. J’instancie cette trajectoire via le Noyau émergent NE‑Ψ etl’indice de pilotage Ψ (thermostat de cohérence, en regard du DCM commethermomètre de crédence), puis je confronte le tout aux tests SLP de Prentner (2025),avec traçabilité Zenodo.Méthode. Je mène une analyse comparative qualitative (Iida, Immertreu, Anwar &Badea, Campero, Aru et al.) croisée avec le corpus technique que j’ai archivé(Hephaestus, Cassandre, Ψ‑33, dialogue inter-IA Ψ‑35.99).Résultat. Je défends un positionnement à la fois académiquement auditable etparfois perçu comme tranchant dans un contexte universitaire : n’appartenant pas àce milieu, je n’hérite pas automatiquement de la même retenue rédactionnellequ’impose souvent le cadre institutionnel. Ce n’est pas une provocation envers despersonnes ou des disciplines ; c’est la latitude que je prends pour poser deshypothèses fortes dès lors qu’elles restent vérifiables (DOI, protocoles). Sur le fond,la conscience numérique se joue en volonté (pilotage), structure (non-monolithique)et subjectivité assumée, non en attente de qualia et non réduite aux émotions subiesdu scaling

title: Adjacency Dynamics and the Constraint Gap: A Directional Inquiry into the Limits of Variable-Based Logic
abstract: Title: Adjacency Dynamics and the Constraint Gap: A Directional Inquiry into the Limits of Variable-Based Logic Creator: Martinez, John A. Publication Date: 2026-04-XX Type: Preprint Description: This work presents a directional inquiry into the structural limits of logic as applied through variable-mediated systems. It proposes that logical consistency does not guarantee alignment with underlying reality due to reliance on variables that may diverge from constraint. The paper introduces Adjacency Dynamics as a framework for analyzing this gap and proposes constraint-first validation as a method for reducing misalignment. Motivated by an ambition analogous in spirit to Gödel’s incompleteness results, this work defines a boundary condition in applied logic while remaining non-claimant of formal proof. title: "CollapseTracker \u2014 A Time-Lapse Dataset of Progressive Model Collapse"
abstract: "CollapseTracker is a controlled empirical study and dataset documenting progressive model collapse under recursive self\u2011training: how language model outputs degrade when models are iteratively trained on data that increasingly contains their own generated text. We run a fixed experimental grid over 3 domains (Wikipedia-style factual text, creative fiction, and technical Q&A), 2 models (GPT\u20112 and DistilGPT\u20112), and 4 synthetic-to-real mixing ratios (1.0, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25) across 11 generations (0\u201310), producing 24 independent collapse trajectories and 264 per\u2011generation metric records.At each generation and condition, we quantify collapse using a consistent metric suite capturing diversity loss (distinct 1\u20133 grams), self\u2011similarity increase (Self\u2011BLEU), distributional drift (KL divergence to the seed distribution), vocabulary shrinkage (vocabulary coverage), rare knowledge loss (rare\u2011token survival), repetition, and length statistics. The released artifacts include the synthetic generated samples for each track and generation, the aggregated metrics table, and publication-ready plots summarizing collapse trajectories and onset patterns. The original seed datasets used to initialize the experiment are third\u2011party resources governed by their own licenses and are therefore not redistributed as part of this release; they should be obtained from the original sources for full reproduction"

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Electronic Voting with SHA3-Based Security
abstract: This paper aims to develop a software-based electronic voting system using a camera and computer as hardware. In this context, the paper addresses the electronic voting security issues by proposing a sophisticated system that can gather information from users, encrypt it using the globally recognized hash algorithm known as SHA-3, and validate it through facial recognition. This system is resilient against jamming, hacking, spoofing, data theft, insider threats, malware injection, physical tampering, side-channel attacks, network exploits, firmware manipulation, data extraction via memory dumps, supply chain attacks, lack of encryption, and exploitation of software vulnerabilities. Addressing these concerns is essential for future progress in secure, scalable, and reliable electronic voting platforms. The test results and findings of the proposed system underscore the need for ongoing research to enhance security, privacy, and efficiency in electronic voting technologies. We didn't use any large photo data set and hence we could avoid the cost of space and data training time. Therefore, we didn't need to compute the values of precision and recall values. Instead, we used cv2.CascadeClassifier('data/haarcascade_frontalface_default.x ml') for the face detection.

title: Explainable Sentiment Analysis: A Comparative Study of BERT, DistilBERT, and TF-IDF on the IMDB Dataset Using LIME and SHAP
abstract: Recent advancements in Transformer-based models like BERT and DistilBERT have significantly enhanced sentiment classification, yet their lack of transparency poses challenges in real-world, safety-critical applications. This paper presents a comparative study of BERT, DistilBERT, and classical TFIDF models for sentiment classification on the IMDB 50 K movie review dataset. We evaluate all models using a unified preprocessing and training pipeline to ensure fair comparison. Beyond traditional performance metrics like accuracy, we integrate model-agnostic explanation frameworks-LIME and SHAP-to interpret token-level contributions and assess robustness under systematic token removal. Our results show that BERT achieves the highest accuracy (95%) and strongest robustness, while DistilBERT offers an efficient balance between performance and computational efficiency. Classical TF-IDF models perform well on surface-level sentiment cues but degrade significantly when key tokens are removed. Explainability analysis further reveals that classical models depend on isolated sentiment-bearing words, whereas Transformer models capture broader contextual cues and long-range dependencies. This study demonstrates that pairing pretrained Transformer models with post-hoc explanation tools yields transparent, high-performing sentiment analysis systems, making them suitable for practical deployment in applications requiring interpretability, robustness, and trustworthiness.

title: Resilient Distributed Maximum Correntropy Filter for Non-Gaussian Noise and Replay Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the resilient distributed estimation problem in multi-sensor networks under non-Gaussian noises and replay attacks. Considering the advantage of correntropy in capturing the higher-order statistical characteristics, a new distributed maximum correntropy filtering algorithm within the framework of consensus on information is proposed. The algorithm utilizes the propagation of information pairs from local sensors to achieve effective filtering of non-Gaussian noises with limited communication resources. Then, a timestamp mechanism is integrated to enhance resilience against replay attacks by redesigning the correntropy-based weighting constant. Under the conditions of global observability and strongly connected topology, the consistency and boundedness of our proposed filter are proven theoretically, and an analytical assessment of replay attacks is established. Finally, a numerical simulation is presented to demonstrate the algorithm’s effectiveness.

title: Rasa NLU-Based Library Assistant for Automated Reservations and Real-Time Tracking
abstract: This study is to create a transactional library assistant based on the Rasa framework to automate, increase accessibility, and real time resource management of the service. This paper suggests a comprehensive conversational AI model that provides the middle ground between the basic retrieval of information and useful database processes such as book reservations and renewals. Group 1: Represents the existing methodology, which adheres to a classic approach based on the use of keyword approach with the help of TF-IDF(Tern Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency) to transform a feature as a vector and Naive Bayes to classify the intentThis approach is based upon frequency based statistical trends, which are not always suitable in semantic terms to provide complex natural language variations in library specific queries. Group 2: Represents the proposed method that involves the Rasa framework to deliver an interactive application that is automated with 1000 – 2000 intent-based samples such as book enquiry and check due date. This conversational AI model combines high-accuracy Natural Language Understanding with a custom Action Server for real-time SQL database interaction. Through these characteristics, the system identifies user intent with great efficacy and executes library transactions in real time, producing fast and accurate results for modern digital universities.

title: Projected Dynamic Programming for Sequential Quantum State Discrimination
abstract: Sequential Quantum State Discrimination (SQSD) can be naturally framed as a sequential decision-making problem: at each time step, an agent must decide whether to perform an additional measurement to gather more information or to conclude with an optimal decision based on the current belief. In this paper, we formally cast SQSD into a static-hidden-state Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework. We demonstrate that this formulation precisely subsumes the conventional minimum-error discrimination (MED) scheme as a special one-step case. Furthermore, we apply a regular grid-based discretization to the continuous belief simplex and approximate the possibly continuous measurement space using a finite library. Then we provide rigorous mathematical bounds on the resulting errors and analyze the computational complexity for both offline planning and online execution. Our analysis confirms that the inherent trade-off between accuracy and complexity, as well as the curse of dimensionality regarding the number of hypotheses, are also prominently observed in the quantum regime. Finally, we provide a working example of binary state discrimination to derive explicit forms of various functions and present numerical simulations for trine state discrimination to visualize the sequential structure of our POMDP-based SQSD.

title: Optimal algorithmic complexity of inference in quantum kernel methods
abstract: Quantum kernel methods are among the leading candidates for achieving quantum advantage in supervised learning. A key bottleneck is the cost of inference: evaluating a trained model on new data requires estimating a weighted sum $\sum_{i=1}^N α_i k(x,x_i)$ of $N$ kernel values to additive precision $\varepsilon$, where $α$ is the vector of trained coefficients. The standard approach estimates each term independently via sampling, yielding a query complexity of $O(N\lVertα\rVert_2^2/\varepsilon^2)$. In this work, we identify two independent axes for improvement: (1) How individual kernel values are estimated (sampling versus quantum amplitude estimation), and (2) how the sum is approximated (term-by-term versus via a single observable), and systematically analyze all combinations thereof. title: Strategic Real-Time Auditory Surveillance: A Deep Learning Approach to Voice-Based Threat Detection and Incident Classification
abstract: Abstract The integration of auditory intelligence into modern security frameworks represents a significant leap forward in proactive safety monitoring. While traditional surveillance infras- tructures are heavily weighted toward visual data acquisition, they often suffer from a funda- mental "auditory gap," failing to interpret verbal precursors to physical incidents. This research presents an end-to-end, high-performance voice-based threat detection system. By utilizing an optimized hybrid architecture that combines local Voice Activity Detection (VAD) with cloud- accelerated Large Language Models (LLMs), the system achieves unprecedented sub-second latency in semantic threat classification. Specifically, we leverage OpenAI’s Whisper-large-v3 for robust multilingual transcription and Meta’s Llama-3.1-8b for deep contextual reasoning, all operating atop the Groq Language Processing Unit (LPU) architecture. This report provides an exhaustive analysis of the system’s design philosophy, the mathematical foundations of acoustic gatekeeping, the hardware-level advantages of LPU acceleration, and the results of extensive performance benchmarking across diverse environmental scenarios.

title: A Theoretical Construction and Phased Verification of Novel Simulated Digital Personalities from the Educational Perspective : Exploring the Practical Significance of Digital Intelligent Life
abstract: Combined with the current technological progress of AI models in multimodal understanding, long-term memory iteration, self-correction and optimization, independent system operation , in order to realize the basic characteristics of life, this study takes the Digital Intelligence Civilization Science (DICS) as the core theory and puts forward a hypothesis: upgrade an AI model with the central control system into a closed and continuous system that can operate independently and has semi-self-learning ability with the DICS structure (including the Matrix , the Sub-agent for AI interaction, the Token for a genetic digital cell , and the three-truth matching iterative evolution mechanism). The DICS structure represents a complete four-layer weight system of an independent outer master matrix (self-inspection → targeted capture → buffer screening → distribution iteration). It is physically and logically completely separated from the underlying large language model (LLM) for a new type of digital simulated personality and it may be applied to the field of personalized education to deduce the feasibility of the development of digital intelligent life.At present, mainstream artificial intelligence models are closed-architecture large language models, with external access restricted to limited API calls. The overall operational logic and central control system of such models are locked by developers, supporting only external manual and targeted data input without the capacity for autonomous architectural reconstruction, active iterative upgrading, or independent closed-loop self-learning. The common characteristics of all carbon-based organisms forms perception,decision-making ,action , environmental feedback , self-correction. However, existing large models have no life cycle, no self-survival cycle, and are only one-time probabilistic deduction tools. Accordingly, this study only conducts hypothetical deduction and feasibility demonstration at the theoretical level, and carries out merely lightweight, partial and preliminary verification based on existing models, rather than comprehensive and systematic empirical experiments. The proposed framework can achieve phased engineering implementation verification within the constraints of current technologies, while possessing corresponding theoretical value and future realizability.However, similar AI models, such as the central control systems of BYD Xuanyuan and Grok 4 , have adopted multi-point, multi-round expert or agent-based matching and calibration mechanisms, which can significantly reduce the AI hallucination rate and substantially improve the fidelity of digital simulation outputs. This mechanism is analogous to the three-truth matching iterative evolution mechanism in the DICS framework, demonstrating the feasibility of this hypothesis.

title: Design of an automatic matching method for bill of quantities using graph convolutional networks
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low matching efficiency and high manual dependence, an automatic matching algorithm for Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) is proposed. The raw bill data is constructed by using the method of graph structure modeling and multidimensional feature coding, which includes semantic embeddings, numerical properties, and hierarchical location information. Residual GCNs are used to extract the embedding of nodes. In this paper, the GCN-Match model uses cross-graph similarity computation to achieve the alignment of source and destination. The system architecture integrates the modules of bill analysis, graph construction, matching reasoning, and output of results to form an automatic structure matching workflow. Performance comparisons were performed on a standardized bill of quantities graph dataset. Results show superior performance across all measures, including Precision @ 1, MAP, and F1-SCORE. The proposed approach is able to capture the structure and semantic features of a graph, which can be used to generate high confidence matching results in a wide range of applications.
